title: Features – Linear

comments.text: Quiet dark surface, almost no colour, the type carries the brand, a tiny mark. Take: restraint, and the product itself as the advertising frame.

thread.answer:
- Linear presents the product development cycle, from roadmap to release, as its central message.
- Planning uses projects and initiatives to set direction; building uses issues and cycles to track progress.
- AI workflows and agents, analytics, and mobile access extend that core workflow.
- Customer Requests and Linear Asks connect incoming requests to product work.
- The closing line, “Plan the present. Build the future,” compresses the product promise into a short statement.
- Claimed, not demonstrated: “best-in-class” security and building what customers actually want.

Sections:
- The system for modern product development — the roadmap-to-release promise.
- Planning — projects and initiatives set direction.
- Building — issue tracking and cycle planning.
- Artificial intelligence — AI-powered workflows and agents.
- Insights — analytics for streams of work.
- Mobile — product work from anywhere.
- Customer Requests — requests inform what gets built.
- Linear Asks — workplace requests become issues.
- Security — a claim about security practices.
- Plan the present. Build the future. — closing line and calls to action.

Terms:
- Projects and initiatives — the planning structures named for setting product direction.
- Issue tracking — the way building work is followed.
- Cycle planning — the planning method paired with issue tracking.
- AI-powered workflows and agents — the named means of streamlining product development.
- Customer Requests — the feature for bringing customer wants into product work.
- Linear Asks — the feature that turns workplace requests into issues.

How to apply:
- Write one sentence that spans your product’s full workflow; the result is a clear central promise.
- Arrange feature copy from direction-setting through day-to-day work; the result is a product-led page outline.
- Give each feature a short name and one concrete outcome; the result is copy that can carry a restrained layout.
- Check superlatives such as “best-in-class” against available evidence; the result is a page without unsupported claims.
